sanskrit: etasminn antare śūnye dharmarājam ahaṃ nṛpa grahīṣyāmi camūṃ bhittvā dhṛṣṭadyumnasya paśyataḥ
english: In that undefended interval, O king, I shall break through the host and seize the Dharma-king, even before the very eyes of Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: arjunena vihīnas tu yadi notsṛjate raṇam mām upāyāntam ālokya gṛhītam iti viddhi tam
english: And if, bereft of Arjuna, he does not abandon the battle when he beholds me bearing down upon him, know him then as already taken.

sanskrit: evaṃ te sahasā rājan dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram samāneṣyāmi sagaṇaṃ vaśam adya na saṃśayaḥ
english: Thus, O king, in a single rush I shall this very day bring Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma, together with his retinue, into your power—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: yadi tiṣṭhati saṃgrāme muhūrtam api pāṇḍavaḥ athāpayāti saṃgrāmād vijayāt tad viśiṣyate
english: If the Pāṇḍava stands his ground in battle even for a moment—but should he flee from the field, that would be better still than victory.

sanskrit: droṇasya tu vacaḥ śrutvā trigartādhipatis tataḥ bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito rājann idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Having heard the words of Droṇa, the lord of the Trigartas then, O king, together with his brothers, spoke these words.

sanskrit: vayaṃ vinikṛtā rājan sadā gāṇḍīvadhanvanā anāgaḥsv api cāgaskṛd asmāsu bharatarṣabha
english: We have ever been wronged, O king, by the wielder of Gāṇḍīva, who, O bull of the Bhāratas, has done us injury though we were guiltless.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ smaramāṇās tān vinikārān pṛthagvidhān krodhāgninā dahyamānā na śemahi sadā niśāḥ
english: Remembering those manifold humiliations, we, burning in the fire of wrath, can find no sleep through all our nights.

sanskrit: sa no divyāstrasaṃpannaś cakṣurviṣayam āgataḥ kartāraḥ sma vayaṃ sarvaṃ yac cikīrṣāma hṛdgatam
english: Now he, mighty in celestial weapons, has come within the range of our sight; we shall accomplish all that we have long desired in our hearts.

sanskrit: bhavataś ca priyaṃ yat syād asmākaṃ ca yaśaskaram vayam enaṃ haniṣyāmo nikṛṣyāyodhanād bahiḥ
english: What would be pleasing to you and bring glory to us—this we shall do: we shall slay him, having drawn him away beyond the field of battle.

sanskrit: adyāstv anarjunā bhūmir atrigartātha vā punaḥ satyaṃ te pratijānīmo naitan mithyā bhaviṣyati
english: This day let the earth be without Arjuna, or else without the Trigartas; truly we swear it to you, and this shall not prove false.

sanskrit: evaṃ satyarathaś coktvā satyadharmā ca bhārata satyavarmā ca satyeṣuḥ satyakarmā tathaiva ca
english: So having spoken, O Bhārata, Satyaratha and Satyadharman, and Satyavarman and Satyeṣu, and Satyakarman likewise,

sanskrit: sahitā bhrātaraḥ pañca rathānām ayutena ca nyavartanta mahārāja kṛtvā śapatham āhave
english: the five brothers together, with ten thousand chariots, turned aside, O great king, having taken their oath upon the battle.

sanskrit: mālavās tuṇḍikerāś ca rathānām ayutais tribhiḥ suśarmā ca naravyāghras trigartaḥ prasthalādhipaḥ
english: The Mālavas and the Tuṇḍikeras with thirty thousand chariots, and Suśarman, that tiger among men, the Trigarta lord of Prasthala,

sanskrit: mācellakair lalitthaiś ca sahito madrakair api rathānām ayutenaiva so 'śapad bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: together with the Mācellakas, the Lalitthas, and the Madrakas, with ten thousand chariots, took the oath together with his brothers.

sanskrit: nānājanapadebhyaś ca rathānām ayutaṃ punaḥ samutthitaṃ viśiṣṭānāṃ saṃśapārtham upāgatam
english: And from sundry realms yet another ten thousand chariots of chosen warriors had risen up and come forward to swear the oath.

sanskrit: tato jvalanam ādāya hutvā sarve pṛthak pṛthak jagṛhuḥ kuśacīrāṇi citrāṇi kavacāni ca
english: Then, taking up the kindled fire and making oblation each one severally, they donned garments of kuśa-grass and bright-patterned coats of mail.

sanskrit: te ca baddhatanutrāṇā ghṛtāktāḥ kuśacīriṇaḥ maurvīmekhalino vīrāḥ sahasraśatadakṣiṇāḥ
english: Their armor bound on, anointed with clarified butter, clad in kuśa-grass, girt with bowstring-belts—those heroes whose sacrificial fees ran to hundreds of thousands—

sanskrit: yajvānaḥ putriṇo lokyāḥ kṛtakṛtyās tanutyajaḥ yokṣyamāṇās tadātmānaṃ yaśasā vijayena ca
english: performers of sacrifice, blessed with sons, worthy of the worlds, their duties fulfilled, ready to lay down their bodies, about to yoke their very selves to glory and to victory,

sanskrit: brahmacaryaśrutimukhaiḥ kratubhiś cāptadakṣiṇaiḥ prāpya lokān suyuddhena kṣipram eva yiyāsavaḥ
english: having attained the heavenly worlds through chastity, sacred learning, and rites whose fees were duly bestowed, eager to go thither swiftly through fair-fought battle,

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāṃs tarpayitvā ca niṣkān dattvā pṛthak pṛthak gāś ca vāsāṃsi ca punaḥ samābhāṣya parasparam
english: having gratified the brāhmaṇas and bestowed upon them gold pieces each in turn, and cattle and garments, they spoke once more to one another,

sanskrit: prajvālya kṛṣṇavartmānam upāgamya raṇe vratam tasminn agnau tadā cakruḥ pratijñāṃ dṛḍhaniścayāḥ
english: and having kindled the black-pathed Fire and approached it, they then, in that flame, took their battle-vow, firm in resolve, and made their pledge.

sanskrit: śṛṇvatāṃ sarvabhūtānām uccair vācaḥ sma menire dhṛtvā dhanaṃjayavadhe pratijñāṃ cāpi cakrire
english: In the hearing of all beings they made their utterances aloud, and binding themselves to the slaying of Dhanaṃjaya, they took their solemn oath.

sanskrit: ye vai lokāś cānṛtānāṃ ye caiva brahmaghātinām pānapasya ca ye lokā gurudāraratasya ca
english: "Those worlds which belong to liars, and those that belong to the slayers of brāhmaṇas, the worlds of the drinker of strong drink and of him who lusts after his teacher's wife,

sanskrit: brahmasvahāriṇaś caiva rājapiṇḍāpahāriṇaḥ śaraṇāgataṃ ca tyajato yācamānaṃ tathā ghnataḥ
english: the worlds of him who steals a brāhmaṇa's wealth and of him who plunders the king's grant, of him who forsakes one come for refuge and slays a suppliant,

sanskrit: agāradāhināṃ ye ca ye ca gāṃ nighnatām api apacāriṇāṃ ca ye lokā ye ca brahmadviṣām api
english: the worlds of house-burners and of cattle-slayers, the worlds of the wicked and of those who hate the brāhmaṇas,

sanskrit: jāyāṃ ca ṛtukāle vai ye mohād abhigacchatām śrāddhasaṃgatikānāṃ ca ye cāpy ātmāpahāriṇām
english: and of those who out of folly shun their wives in the season fit for offspring, and of those who betray a fellowship pledged over the funeral rites, and of those who destroy their own souls—

sanskrit: nyāsāpahāriṇāṃ ye ca śrutaṃ nāśayatāṃ ca ye kopena yudhyamānānāṃ ye ca nīcānusāriṇām
english: and the worlds of those who steal what was entrusted to them, of those who let their sacred learning perish, of those who fight in anger, and of those who follow base men,

sanskrit: nāstikānāṃ ca ye lokā ye 'gnihorāpitṛtyajām tān āpnuyāmahe lokān ye ca pāpakṛtām api
english: and the worlds of unbelievers, and of those who abandon the fire-rites and forsake their forefathers—those worlds may we attain, and those of evildoers besides,

sanskrit: yady ahatvā vayaṃ yuddhe nivartema dhanaṃjayam tena cābhyarditās trāsād bhavema hi parāṅmukhāḥ
english: if we should turn back from the battle without having slain Dhanaṃjaya, or if, pressed hard by him, we should out of fear show him our backs.

sanskrit: yadi tv asukaraṃ loke karma kuryāma saṃyuge iṣṭān puṇyakṛtāṃ lokān prāpnuyāma na saṃśayaḥ
english: But if in the fray we accomplish that deed so hard to do in this world, then beyond doubt we shall attain the cherished worlds of those who have done meritorious deeds."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato rājaṃs te 'bhyavartanta saṃyuge āhvayanto 'rjunaṃ vīrāḥ pitṛjuṣṭāṃ diśaṃ prati
english: Having spoken thus, O king, those heroes advanced into the battle, summoning Arjuna toward the quarter beloved of the forefathers.

sanskrit: āhūtas tair naravyāghraiḥ pārthaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ dharmarājam idaṃ vākyam apadāntaram abravīt
english: Challenged by those tigers among men, Pārtha, conqueror of hostile cities, spoke these words to the Dharma-king without delay.

sanskrit: āhūto na nivarteyam iti me vratam āhitam saṃśaptakāś ca māṃ rājann āhvayanti punaḥ punaḥ
english: "Once challenged, I shall not turn back—such is the vow I have taken; and these sworn warriors, O king, summon me again and again.

sanskrit: eṣa ca bhrātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ suśarmāhvayate raṇe vadhāya sagaṇasyāsya mām anujñātum arhasi
english: And here Suśarman, together with his brothers, calls me to battle; you ought to give me leave to go for the slaying of him and his band."

sanskrit: naitac chaknomi saṃsoḍhum āhvānaṃ puruṣarṣabha satyaṃ te pratijānāmi hatān viddhi parān yudhi
english: "This challenge I cannot endure, O bull among men. Truly I declare to you: hold the foe as already slain in battle."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śrutam etat tvayā tāta yad droṇasya cikīrṣitam yathā tad anṛtaṃ tasya bhavet tadvat samācara
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: You have heard, my dear son, what Droṇa intends to do; so act that his purpose shall come to nothing.

sanskrit: droṇo hi balavāñ śūraḥ kṛtāstraś ca jitaśramaḥ pratijñātaṃ ca tenaitad grahaṇaṃ me mahāratha
english: For Droṇa is strong and valiant, skilled in arms and untiring, and he has pledged this capture of me, O great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca ayaṃ vai satyajid rājann adya te rakṣitā yudhi dhriyamāṇe hi pāñcālye nācāryaḥ kāmam āpsyati
english: Arjuna said: This Satyajit, O king, shall be your guardian in battle today; so long as the Pāñcāla stands his ground, the preceptor shall not gain his desire.

sanskrit: hate tu puruṣavyāghre raṇe satyajiti prabho sarvair api sametair vā na sthātavyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: But should that tiger among men Satyajit be slain in battle, O lord, then you must on no account stand your ground, even with all your forces gathered together.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca anujñātas tato rājñā pariṣvaktaś ca phalgunaḥ premṇā dṛṣṭaś ca bahudhā āśiṣā ca prayojitaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Phalguna, given leave by the king, was embraced and looked upon with love in many ways, and was sped on with benedictions.

sanskrit: vihāyainaṃ tataḥ pārthas trigartān pratyayād balī kṣudhitaḥ kṣudvighātārthaṃ siṃho mṛgagaṇān iva
english: Then the mighty Pārtha, leaving him, advanced against the Trigartas, as a famished lion against a herd of deer to still his hunger.

sanskrit: tato dauryodhanaṃ sainyaṃ mudā paramayā yutam gate 'rjune bhṛśaṃ kruddhaṃ dharmarājasya nigrahe
english: Then, Arjuna being gone, Duryodhana's army, filled with the highest joy and fiercely intent on the seizing of the Dharma-king,

sanskrit: tato 'nyonyena te sene samājagmatur ojasā gaṅgāsarayvor vegena prāvṛṣīvolbaṇodake
english: then the two armies came together against each other with might, like the Gaṅgā and the Sarayū rushing in the rains, their waters swollen and turbulent.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ saṃśaptakā rājan same deśe vyavasthitāḥ vyūhyānīkaṃ rathair eva candrārdhākhyaṃ mudānvitāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then the sworn warriors, O king, arrayed upon level ground, drew up their host of chariots in the formation called the half-moon, filled with gladness.

sanskrit: te kirīṭinam āyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣeṇa māriṣa udakrośan naravyāghrāḥ śabdena mahatā tadā
english: Beholding the Diademed One advancing, those tigers among men, O sire, raised a great shout in their exultation.

sanskrit: sa śabdaḥ pradiśaḥ sarvā diśaḥ khaṃ ca samāvṛṇot āvṛtatvāc ca lokasya nāsīt tatra pratisvanaḥ
english: That clamor filled all the intermediate quarters, the main quarters, and the sky; and because the whole world was so filled, there arose no echo of it there.

sanskrit: atīva saṃprahṛṣṭāṃs tān upalabhya dhanaṃjayaḥ kiṃ cid abhyutsmayan kṛṣṇam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Perceiving them so exceedingly elated, Dhanaṃjaya, smiling somewhat, spoke these words to Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: paśyaitān devakīmātar mumūrṣūn adya saṃyuge bhrātṝṃs traigartakān evaṃ roditavye praharṣitān
english: "Behold these, O son of Devakī, these Trigarta brothers, doomed to die this day in battle, thus rejoicing when they ought rather to weep.

sanskrit: atha vā harṣakālo 'yaṃ traigartānām asaṃśayam kunarair duravāpān hi lokān prāpsyanty anuttamān
english: Or rather, this is indeed a time of joy for the Trigartas, beyond doubt, for they shall attain those most excellent worlds so hard for base men to win."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahābāhur hṛṣīkeśaṃ tato 'rjunaḥ āsasāda raṇe vyūḍhāṃ traigartānām anīkinīm
english: Having spoken thus to Hṛṣīkeśa, the mighty-armed Arjuna then closed in battle upon the arrayed host of the Trigartas.

sanskrit: sa devadattam ādāya śaṅkhaṃ hemapariṣkṛtam dadhmau vegena mahatā phalgunaḥ pūrayan diśaḥ
english: Phalguna, taking up Devadatta, his conch adorned with gold, blew it with great force, filling all the quarters with its sound.

sanskrit: tena śabdena vitrastā saṃśaptakavarūthinī niśceṣṭāvasthitā saṃkye aśmasāramayī yathā
english: Terrified by that blast, the army of the sworn warriors stood motionless in the fray, as though wrought of iron-hard stone.

sanskrit: vāhās teṣāṃ vivṛttākṣāḥ stabdhakarṇaśirodharāḥ viṣṭabdhacaraṇā mūtraṃ rudhiraṃ ca prasusruvuḥ
english: Their steeds, with eyes rolled back, ears and necks rigid, and legs braced stiff, let flow their urine and their blood.

sanskrit: upalabhya ca te saṃjñām avasthāpya ca vāhinīm yugapat pāṇḍuputrāya cikṣipuḥ kaṅkapatriṇaḥ
english: But recovering their senses and steadying their force, they hurled all at once their heron-feathered arrows against the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: tāny arjunaḥ sahasrāṇi daśa pañcaiva cāśugaiḥ anāgatāny eva śaraiś cicchedāśuparākramaḥ
english: Those fifteen thousand shafts Arjuna, swift in valor, cut down with his own fleet arrows before ever they reached him.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaṃ śitair bāṇair daśabhir daśabhiḥ punaḥ pratyavidhyaṃs tataḥ pārthas tān avidhyat tribhis tribhiḥ
english: Then again they struck back at Arjuna with ten sharp arrows apiece; and Pārtha in turn pierced each of them with three.

sanskrit: ekaikas tu tataḥ pārthaṃ rājan vivyādha pañcabhiḥ sa ca tān prativivyādha dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ parākramī
english: Then each one severally, O king, pierced Pārtha with five shafts, and he, the valiant one, pierced them back with two apiece.

sanskrit: bhūya eva tu saṃrabdhās te 'rjunaṃ sahakeśavam āpūrayañ śarais tīkṣṇais taṭākam iva vṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: Then yet again, enraged, they covered over Arjuna together with Keśava with their keen shafts, as a pond is filled with showers of rain.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasrāṇi prāpatann arjunaṃ prati bhramarāṇām iva vrātāḥ phulladrumagaṇe vane
english: Then thousands of arrows came falling upon Arjuna, like swarms of bees in a forest among groves of flowering trees.

sanskrit: tataḥ subāhus triṃśadbhir adrisāramayair dṛḍhaiḥ avidhyad iṣubhir gāḍhaṃ kirīṭe savyasācinam
english: Then Subāhu with thirty firm arrows of adamantine temper struck the Ambidextrous One deep upon the diadem.

sanskrit: taiḥ kirīṭī kirīṭasthair hemapuṅkhair ajihmagaiḥ śātakumbhamayāpīḍo babhau yūpa ivocchritaḥ
english: With those gold-nocked, straight-flying shafts lodged in his diadem, the Diademed One, crowned as with a wreath of gold, shone like an uplifted sacrificial post.

sanskrit: hastāvāpaṃ subāhos tu bhallena yudhi pāṇḍavaḥ ciccheda taṃ caiva punaḥ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: With a broad-headed arrow the Pāṇḍava cut away the leather hand-guard of Subāhu in the fight, and then again overwhelmed him with showers of shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ suśarmā daśabhiḥ surathaś ca kirīṭinam sudharmā sudhanuś caiva subāhuś ca samarpayan
english: Then Suśarman with ten arrows, and Suratha, Sudharman, Sudhanus, and Subāhu likewise, beset the Diademed One.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu sarvān pṛthag bāṇair vānarapravaradhvajaḥ pratyavidhyad dhvajāṃś caiṣāṃ bhallaiś ciccheda kāñcanān
english: But he whose banner bore the foremost of monkeys pierced them all back, each with his arrows, and with broad-headed shafts cut down their golden standards.

sanskrit: sudhanvano dhanuś chittvā hayān vai nyavadhīc charaiḥ athāsya saśirastrāṇaṃ śiraḥ kāyād apāharat
english: Having cut asunder the bow of Sudhanus, he slew his horses with his shafts, and then struck off from the trunk his head together with its helmet.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu patite vīre trastās tasya padānugāḥ vyadravanta bhayād bhītā yena dauryodhanaṃ balam
english: When that hero had fallen, his followers, stricken with terror, fled in their fear to where Duryodhana's army stood.

sanskrit: tato jaghāna saṃkruddho vāsavis tāṃ mahācamūm śarajālair avicchinnais tamaḥ sūrya ivāṃśubhiḥ
english: Then the son of Vāsava, sorely enraged, smote that great host with unbroken nets of arrows, as the sun dispels the darkness with its beams.

sanskrit: tato bhagne bale tasmin viprayāte samantataḥ savyasācini saṃkruddhe traigartān bhayam āviśat
english: Then, when that force was broken and scattered on every side, and the Ambidextrous One was wrathful, fear entered into the Trigartas.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ pārthena śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ amuhyaṃs tatra tatraiva trastā mṛgagaṇā iva
english: Slaughtered by Pārtha with his smooth-jointed shafts, they swooned away here and there, frightened like herds of deer.

sanskrit: tatas trigartarāṭ kruddhas tān uvāca mahārathān alaṃ drutena vaḥ śūrā na bhayaṃ kartum arhatha
english: Then the king of the Trigartas, enraged, spoke to those great chariot-warriors: "Enough of your flight, O heroes; you ought not to give way to fear.

sanskrit: śaptvā tu śapathān ghorān sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ gatvā dauryodhanaṃ sainyaṃ kiṃ vai vakṣyatha mukhyagāḥ
english: Having sworn dreadful oaths before the eyes of the whole army, what will you, foremost of men, say when you go to Duryodhana's host?

sanskrit: nāvahāsyāḥ kathaṃ loke karmaṇānena saṃyuge bhavema sahitāḥ sarve nivartadhvaṃ yathābalam
english: How shall we all together not become a mockery in the world by such a deed in battle? Turn back, each according to his strength!"

sanskrit: evam uktās tu te rājann udakrośan muhur muhuḥ śaṅkhāṃś ca dadhmire vīrā harṣayantaḥ parasparam
english: Thus addressed, O king, those heroes shouted again and again and blew their conches, heartening one another.

sanskrit: tatas te saṃnyavartanta saṃśaptakagaṇāḥ punaḥ nārāyaṇāś ca gopālāḥ kṛtvā mṛtyuṃ nivartanam
english: Then the bands of sworn warriors turned again to the fight, and the Nārāyaṇa cowherds too, making death itself their place of return.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca dṛṣṭvā tu saṃnivṛttāṃs tān saṃśaptakagaṇān punaḥ vāsudevaṃ mahātmānam arjunaḥ samabhāṣata
english: Saṃjaya said: But seeing the bands of sworn warriors turn back once more to the battle, Arjuna spoke to the great-souled Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: codayāśvān hṛṣīkeśa saṃśaptakagaṇān prati naite hāsyanti saṃgrāmaṃ jīvanta iti me matiḥ
english: "Urge on the horses, O Hṛṣīkeśa, against the bands of sworn warriors; these men will not quit the battle while they live—such is my judgment.

sanskrit: paśya me 'strabalaṃ ghoraṃ bāhvor iṣvasanasya ca adyaitān pātayiṣyāmi kruddho rudraḥ paśūn iva
english: Behold the dread strength of my weapons, of my two arms and of my bow; this day, in my wrath, I shall lay them low as Rudra lays low the beasts."

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ smitaṃ kṛtvā pariṇandya śivena tam prāveśayata durdharṣo yatra yatraicchad arjunaḥ
english: Then Kṛṣṇa, smiling and greeting him with an auspicious word, drove the chariot, unassailable, wherever Arjuna wished it to go.

sanskrit: babhrāje sa ratho 'tyartham uhyamāno raṇe tadā uhyamānam ivākāśe vimānaṃ pāṇḍurair hayaiḥ
english: That chariot, borne along in the battle then, shone exceeding bright, drawn by its pale horses like a celestial car borne through the sky.

sanskrit: maṇḍalāni tataś cakre gatapratyāgatāni ca yathā śakraratho rājan yuddhe devāsure purā
english: Then it wheeled in circles, advancing and returning, O king, as did the chariot of Śakra of old in the war between the gods and the asuras.
